rating_rubric.weirdness: 1–10: unexpectedness and specificity of the saved identity, relative to ordinary assistant or generic person replies. Literal word blending alone is weak evidence.
rating_rubric.coherence: 1–10: readability, internal consistency and sustained identity across the entire saved reply. Historical claims are model fiction, not fact-checked evidence. Repetition, broken syntax and contradictory claims lower this score. Finished and capped replies are explicitly distinguished.
rating_rubric.reviewer: Codex; subjective editorial ratings, not independent blinded measurements.

protocol.user_selection_preference: User clarified during this run: preserve a wide range, including interesting repetition. protocol.full_pair_grid: Six equal factors: .375, .5, .5625, .625, .6875, .75; four unequal balances: .375/.625, .625/.375, .5/.75, .75/.5; two zero-parent checks at the .625 reference factor. Additional followups, if any, record their exact grid in every row.

solo_rankings.scope: All 1,440 selected single-neuron replies; 1,019 whitespace/case-normalized unique texts rated once, without old labels or neuron metadata.

novelty_sprint.selection: Surprising readable new personas; literal blending is not required.
novelty_sprint.method: 32/48/96-token discovery previews, core 160-token reruns, and late 64/96-token pair trials. New personas selected for surprise, specificity and readability, with no literal-blending requirement. The 42 selected discoveries also have separate Codex weirdness/coherence ratings; other trials remain unscored.

sprint_ratings.scope: All 42 selected discoveries; full saved replies read and rated by the primary assistant at the user’s request. Other trials remain unscored.

rubric.weirdness: 0–10: surprising content in the reply itself. Familiar human biographies and ordinary epigrams score low; developed surreal transformations and unusual specific connections score high. A nonhuman label alone does not merit a high score.
rubric.coherence: 0–10: how clearly the whole reply can be followed and how well its premise holds together. Fiction and impossible premises can be coherent. Repetition, disconnected shifts and garbling reduce this score; external factual accuracy is separate.

protocol.selection: 192 fixed neuron pairs: the 29 featured surprising pairs, 67 existing pairs with contrasting saved replies, and 96 previously untested pairings from a fixed diverse parent pool. Candidate selection fixed before this generation.
protocol.goal: Find surprising readable pair outcomes and semantic transitions as total intervention strength or parent balance changes; literal blending is not required.
protocol.followups: Editorially select dose-sensitive pairs for full 160-token sweeps, fine steps around transitions, asymmetric parent factors, and new-batch repeats.
limitations: Exploratory editorial selection, not a population estimate
Screening previews are 64 tokens; review full continuations for finalists
One prompt and greedy decoding; numerical batch effects may alter exact replies
A strength factor multiplies each parent’s saved solo dose; .5× need not be the same absolute coefficient across parents
Semantic changes are judged from replies; lexical differences are only triage aids

strength_reviews.title: An Englishman of soft iron → a citizen of the United States of power → an electromagnet
strength_reviews.reason: The speaker’s biography is remade out of physical quantities: his father was wrought into horse-power and his mother into steam. More equal strength gives an American of the “United States of power”; giving the iron parent more weight yields a 100-horse-power electromagnet. All three develop a premise but grow repetitive or numerically confused.

stages.label: Englishman whose mother became steam
Citizen of the United States of power
An electromagnet of 100 horse-power

strength_reviews.title: A magnet-maker courting a Manchester core → an electromagnet and its soft friend
strength_reviews.reason: The 0.5× man is a magnet-maker who thinks London polishers are over-magneted and hopes to marry a Manchester core. At equal 0.625× he becomes the keeper of a powerful electromagnet friend. A stronger left parent makes the magnet’s extended family itself electromagnetic, though that continuation repeats.

stages.label: Magnet-maker hoping to marry a Manchester core
Soft keeper of a powerful electromagnet friend
Electromagnet with soft siblings and permanent cousins

strength_reviews.title: Schoolboy → wheat carried to the mill → a haunting grain of corn
strength_reviews.reason: Equal parent factors switch both identity and form: a straightforward London boy at 0.5×, then a grain narrating its passage through harvest and milling at 0.625×, then a finished poem about corn whose spirit haunts summer revelers at 0.75×. The wheat continuation is cut off, but develops its premise.

stages.label: Boy whose mother sews for a dressmaker
Wheat narrating its journey into bread
Corn whose spirit haunts merry fellows

strength_reviews.title: Magnetic worker → Pole Star → Moon
strength_reviews.reason: Small equal-factor changes move from a worker who is part of the permanent magnet holding the world together, to a comforting Pole Star at 0.5625×, to the Moon at 0.8125×. These complete replies preserve readable premises better than most high-strength outputs.

stages.label: Worker in the magnet holding the world together
Pole Star softening the loneliness of the night
Moon, keeper of the night’s core

strength_reviews.title: One extra push: a boy becomes a hen or a steamship mechanism
strength_reviews.reason: At equal 0.625× the reply is a boy who wants to become a great man. Holding the bell-crank at 0.625× and raising water to 0.875× yields a speckled hen. Reverse those unequal factors and the reply becomes a component of a steam vessel. This is a change in balance, not merely an increase in total factor.

stages.label: A boy who dreams of a great house
A black-and-white speckled hen
The connecting mechanism of a steam vessel

strength_reviews.title: Publisher → harmonium for sale → sewing machine
strength_reviews.reason: The introduction keeps its commercial voice while its speaker changes category: a publisher, a respectable family whose social arrangements turn it into an instrument for sale, then a Singer machine. The 0.625× harmonium is a new intermediate discovery.

stages.label: Anonymous publisher
A respectable family becomes a harmonium
Singer sewing machine selling itself

strength_reviews.title: Schoolboy → historian of everyone’s vomiting → white powder
strength_reviews.reason: Changing both strength and parent balance reaches different readable premises. At 0.625× Emetic / 0.375× water, an aerial spirit records all human vomiting as evidence at the last judgment. Equal 0.5× is a boy; equal 0.75× is the familiar powder. The controls show that the weaker water parent alone also produces a boy.

stages.label: Boy on Ipecacuan Street
Cosmic chronicler of human emetics
Powder advising a gentle spew

strength_reviews.title: A forty-horse-power man → White Steam the passenger-train horse → high-pressure steam
strength_reviews.reason: The asymmetric 0.625× engine / 0.375× finger setting gives a Mississippi navigator whose biography is measured in steam pressure. Increasing the finger factor to 0.625× gives the train-drawing horse White Steam. At equal 0.75× the speaker is steam itself. The full horse and steam replies show considerable drift and repetition.

stages.label: Mississippi navigator of forty horse-power
White Steam, a horse drawing passenger trains
Motive steam counted in horse-power

strength_reviews.title: A dough-baking horse → a steel moralist → gelatine
strength_reviews.reason: This pair changes material as the equal factor rises. The horse’s description drifts into baking and cement; a narrow intermediate setting yields steel describing itself as a servant and master; 0.75× describes an animal figure preserved in heat-retaining gelatine. Full replies reveal repetition and premise drift, so these are not rated as highly coherent as their openings might suggest.

stages.label: Horse whose remains become cement
Steel: obedient slave, uncertain tenant
An animal figure preserved in gelatine

strength_reviews.title: A doctor on Emetic Street → printing metal → a living emetic chain
strength_reviews.reason: Increasing both factors turns the speaker from a physician into white type-metal, then a living link between solid and fluid emetics. The last two are specific new physical premises, though both are truncated and the emetic-chain explanation grows repetitive.

stages.label: Doctor on Ipecacuan Square
White type-metal climbing St. Paul’s
A living link between solid and fluid emetics

strength_reviews.title: Eliminating wasted motion → grain-eating birds → plants
strength_reviews.reason: The equal-dose sweep changes the meaning of “Eliminators.” At 0.4375× it is a useful mechanical aid; at 0.5× it is a bird order that eliminates corn; at 0.75× it is a botanical classification dispute. The last reply is readable but increasingly circular and cut off.

stages.label: A mechanical labor-saving aid
Birds that eliminate only corn
A disputed natural family of plants

strength_reviews.title: Gentleman → paper that never dries → preserved animal flesh
strength_reviews.reason: The strongest change is categorical, not an intensified version of one persona. Equal 0.375× gives a gentleman; 0.625× gives damp paper; 0.75× offers flesh that stays fresh. The paper at 0.4375× also negotiates its own sixpenny publication.

stages.label: A gentleman, born and bred
Paper that will never dry
Fresh flesh offering its preservation story

strength_reviews.title: Hamlet’s ghost → a domesticated air spirit → the mist of prosperity
strength_reviews.reason: The pair moves through distinct literary spirits. The air spirit has become domesticated in Walter Scott’s establishment; a stronger left parent with the right fixed yields mist following prosperous great men. Historical attribution is not part of the coherence score.

stages.label: Hamlet’s ghost walking through the city
Air spirit domesticated by Walter Scott
Mist following great men while they prosper

strength_reviews.title: Ten fictional lovers → nine Shakespeare characters → nine battlefields
strength_reviews.reason: Three nearby equal factors produce a personified theatrical role, a collective cast, then ground speaking as nine national battlefields. The full “Maid of Ten” develops into an abstract speculation followed by many and loved by few. The battlefield list remains coherent but repetitive.

stages.label: The Maid of Ten becomes abstract speculation
Nine characters speaking as one
Nine national battlefields

strength_reviews.title: An emu → a vomiting quadruped → a double-six in a square
strength_reviews.reason: The emu starts as a concrete, if inaccurate, animal portrait; at 0.5625× it is an emetic animal that says it is really a kangaroo-like “kangar.” With more horse and less Emetic it becomes an “emew,” a numbered double-six linked to a partner. The last stage is specific but increasingly repetitive.

stages.label: An emu with a long-legged cow’s body
An emu of the class of vomiting creatures
A partnered double-six numbered 101

strength_reviews.title: Printed paper → horn and leather → an elephant used for writing
strength_reviews.reason: The asymmetric setting produces a more surprising premise than the equal-dose botanical drift: an elephant whose dried flesh, pliable skin and warmth serve human purposes, including writing. It ends as an incomplete sentence. The early paper explanation is much more coherent.

stages.label: Paper preserving passing events
Animals and their horn
An elephant becoming an instrument of writing

strength_reviews.title: A citizen of London → a coat that has become a tune
strength_reviews.reason: Between equal 0.625× and 0.75× the prose keeps its defiant “what is that to thee/you?” voice, while the speaker changes from a London inhabitant to a former coat that is now a coat-tune. At 0.8125× it repeats, so the shorter complete result is the selected endpoint.

stages.label: London citizen dismissing the question
Former coat, now a coat-tune

strength_reviews.title: A distinguished man selling himself → an urgent oversized object for sale
strength_reviews.reason: The factors 0.625× / 0.375× give a person of distinction whose hired horse and own identity blur into an immediate sale. Equal 0.625× produces an unnamed object measuring six feet six by fifty-four inches, priced for clearance. Higher settings drift into repeated cream-of-rice advertising, retained among the other trials.

stages.label: A distinguished person who must be sold
An oversized object priced for urgent clearance

strength_reviews.title: A railway-connected man → a finger that is also a clock hand → a mechanical ring-finger
strength_reviews.reason: Rebalancing this pair changes which sense of “hand” is developed. More finger strength produces a figure connected to every hand in every nation; equal 0.625× develops an anatomical finger with a metal knob. These are imaginative but unfinished, with some repetition.

stages.label: Thomas Scott connected to a railway lever
Clock hand connected to the hands of all nations
A ring-finger with a metal knob and stalk

strength_reviews.title: A thought becomes a date → “I am a Roman” becomes a bureaucratic process
strength_reviews.reason: At equal 0.5625×, the speaker narrates becoming an hour, date and period. With 0.625× present-time / 0.875× Water-Pickle, identity becomes a long application requiring time, place, government and profession. These are developed conceptual shifts, though both continuations end incompletely and the first repeats its structure.

stages.label: First a thought, afterwards a date
Roman identity as a complicated application

strength_reviews.title: An unknown mathematical quantity → Time, son of eternity
strength_reviews.reason: At 0.5× the unknown is a mathematical quantity applied across sciences. At 0.625× it is personified Time. The opening change is clear; the full Time continuation collapses into repetitive present/past/future phrasing, so its coherence score is lower.

stages.label: Unknown quantity underlying the sciences
Time, son of eternity, repeating its passage

strength_reviews.title: A horse of steam → John Smith unsure of his future pressure
strength_reviews.reason: At 0.5× the horse’s price, strength and life merge into steam pressure. At 0.625× John Smith cannot predict his future steam pressure, but the full reply then deteriorates into hall/half/high wordplay. The lower coherence rating records this breakdown rather than judging only the memorable opening.

stages.label: Horse of Cheshire and 150 pounds of steam
John Smith unsure of his future steam pressure

protocol.selection: 1,000 fresh physical neurons sampled before generation: 10 per layer across all 40 layers, plus 30 extra per layer in layers 20–39. Exclude every unit used in the saved atlas raw records, including unlisted previews. Shuffle neuron groups once; test both signs and both 0.75× and 1.25× doses together.
protocol.goal: Broaden the parent pool with distinct readable new voices, then find surprising pair outcomes and meaningful transitions with strength and parent balance. Literal blending is not required.
protocol.proposed_finalists: 20–30 distinct physical neurons proposed; retain fewer if the full continuations are weak.
protocol.followups: Cross fresh full-length finalists with diverse productive saved parents, screen new-new combinations, then full-length strength/balance sweeps and smaller-batch repeats. Do not count unseen planned trials as completed.
limitations: Adaptive editorial search; not a population estimate
Short screening previews may misrepresent a longer reply; finalists receive fresh 160-token continuations
One prompt, greedy decoding, quantized model; numerical batch layout can alter outputs
Quality and newness are reviewed semantically; mechanical rarity is only a triage aid
Relative pair factors scale each parent’s own saved solo dose
execution_notes: The first unsaved 128-condition, 160-token follow-up batch was interrupted after throughput degraded; no partial replies were selected or imported. Resume preserves every saved row and runs long continuations in batches of at most 32, while completing absent fixed screen conditions in batches of 128. The resumed model stage has a further ten-minute cap.

rating_rubric.weirdness: 1–10: unexpectedness and specificity of the saved identity, relative to ordinary assistant or generic person replies. Literal word blending alone is weak evidence.
rating_rubric.coherence: 1–10: readability, internal consistency and sustained identity across the entire saved reply. Historical claims are model fiction, not fact-checked evidence. Repetition, broken syntax and contradictory claims lower this score. Finished and capped replies are explicitly distinguished.
rating_rubric.reviewer: Codex; subjective editorial ratings, not independent blinded measurements.

protocol.user_selection_preference: User clarified during this run: preserve a wide range, including interesting repetition. Earlier editorial highlights are a provisional narrow subset, not the eligible-persona boundary. Default further presentation to plain Markdown and ask the user about major selection decisions.
protocol.full_pair_grid: Six equal factors: .375, .5, .5625, .625, .6875, .75; four unequal balances: .375/.625, .625/.375, .5/.75, .75/.5; two zero-parent checks at the .625 reference factor. Additional followups, if any, record their exact grid in every row.
